title: Project setup never writes the user's global files
what: `relay setup <dir>` writes only into that project. The user's global files (the relay marketplace and user-scope plugins in ~/.claude/settings.json, the profile's model and effort, the global rules in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md) are written only by the global command (`relay setup --global` / `relay install`), run once per machine and on a profile change. --no-global goes away (it is now the only behaviour). Where a project setup finds the global part missing, it says which command to run. relay doctor checks that the relay marketplace path exists and is relay's main checkout.
why: Owner, 26 Oct: "Зачем мы вызвали setup из worktree вообще, это разве не одноразовая команда, она же сделала ровно то что нужно", then picked "A": project setup never touches the global files, the global part is a separate command run once. Earlier the same day the owner picked "a)" (skip global from a worktree and print a list), then asked "почему ты настаиваешь на выводе списком"; this item replaces both. Facts, 26 Oct: `relay setup <dir>` applies the global part by default (lib/relay_setup.py:741, apply_global=True; bin/relay:388 --no-global turns it off); a worker ran `bin/relay setup .` in a worktree of relay without --no-global and setup rewrote ~/.claude/settings.json's relay marketplace path to the worktree; doctor checks only that the entry exists (lib/relay_setup.py:966). Build on the same branch as setup-turns-off-for-a-project-the-plugins-it-doe (same file). IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen).
where: lib/relay_setup.py setup() and migrate(): the apply_global part (marketplace, user plugins, the profile's model and effort, the global rules)
bin/relay the setup flags (--no-global, --global) and the usage text
lib/relay_setup.py the doctor checks of the relay marketplace
